answer.rationale: We cannot roll back (security patch locked, b6 shows gated canary works but does not apply to a revert already ruled out) and the problem is on the write path, so read replica offload (b5) does not address the p99 climb. Failover (b2) is a heavy move for a write-path regression and risks losing in-flight settlement writes at peak. Adding capacity (b3) is about absorbing a known surge in advance; we have no evidence this is a throughput ceiling, and at peak traffic it is the riskiest intervention. Circuit breakers on the payments dependency (b4) is the lowest-blast-radius action that directly targets a write-path hot spot: b4’s archived record confirms containing a partner-side failure preserved the rest of the checkout path while writes kept flowing. If the climb is driven by a downstream dependency hanging or timing out, failing fast will shed latency on the write path immediately, which is exactly what the objective requires.
